Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 98, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Bayyinah (The Clear Proof), because the word "al-bayyinah" occurs in it. Bayyinah means proof and evidence, and the intended meaning here is the Qur'an. The word does not occur in the definite form (ma'rifah) in any other surah.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To rebuke the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists for their denial of the Qur'an and of the Messenger (ﷺ), to express wonder at the contradiction in their condition, and to refute their claim that God obligated them to hold fast to the religions they follow. It also speaks of their destiny and the destiny of the believers in contrast to them.

• The command to devote worship sincerely to God alone, and to intend the Face of God, glorified and exalted be He, in all statements and actions.

[The Tafsir]

The disbelievers among the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists were not going to abandon their disbelief until there came to them the clear sign (al-'alamah) that they had been promised in the earlier Scriptures.
It is the Messenger of God, Muhammad (ﷺ), who recites a Qur'an in purified pages.
In those scriptures are true reports and just commands, which guide to the truth and to the straight path.

The Jews and Christians who were given the Scripture did not differ concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) being a true messenger, because they found his description in their own Scripture. They only differed after it had become clear to them that he is the Prophet whom they had been promised in the Torah and the Gospel. They had been united in affirming the truth of his prophethood, but when he was sent, they split: some of them believed in him, and others denied his prophethood out of envy and spite.

In all the revealed laws, they were commanded only to worship God alone, directing their worship to Him sincerely, turning away from polytheism (shirk) toward faith, to establish the prayer (salah), and to give the obligatory charity (zakat). That is the religion of uprightness, which is Islam.

Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and the polytheists will have as their punishment the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They are the worst of creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 98, verse 7:

Indeed, those who believed in Allah, followed His Messenger, and did righteous deeds, those are the best of creation.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 98, verse 8:

Their reward with their Lord on the Day of Resurrection will be Gardens of Eternal Residence (jannat iqamah) and stability, in the utmost beauty, through whose palaces and trees rivers flow. They will abide therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, accepting their righteous deeds, and they are pleased with Him for what He has prepared for them of various kinds of honours. That is the good reward for those who fear Allah and avoid His disobedience.
